note: A 25-page Mars-colony paper with two drawing tools and two numbering habits. Four MATLAB screenshots carry the only figure captions in the paper, all printed below their artwork with the single form 'Figure N:'; five vector charts - two scatters, a Lorenz curve and two migration curves - print with no caption and no number at all, and are tied down by deixis instead ('We see in the figure below', 'The lower curve above', 'This graph shows'). The four tables use the same colon form, print their captions above their grids, and are uniformly boxed with a rule under the header and between every body row, unshaded, unmerged, with no note line and no continuation. One cross-reference is wrong: the sentence printed over Table 3 says 'summarized in Table 4', which leaves Table 3 uncited and Table 4 announced twice. The two chart dialects are stable within themselves - the screenshots title their plots and print plain integers, the vector charts put the axis title at the end of the axis and print space-separated thousands - and the one pair a reader will compare, Figures 3 and 4, shares no axis word on either side.
rules: One numbering form covers every captioned exhibit - 'Figure N:' and 'Table N:' with a colon - so the paper has a single label grammar across both exhibit kinds [caption.numbering].
Caption side follows the exhibit type, not the part of the paper: all four figure captions print BELOW their artwork and all four table captions print ABOVE their grid [caption.position].

Five of the nine figures print no caption and no number at all - the two scatters on p10, the Lorenz curve on p13 and the two migration curves on pp20-21 - so a reader who trusts the numbering will believe the paper has four figures [caption.verbatim].

The captioned/uncaptioned boundary is a drawing-tool boundary: every captioned figure is a raster MATLAB screenshot and every uncaptioned chart is a vector plot with no frame whose axis titles sit at the axis ends, so the tool that drew the exhibit decided whether it got a number [geometry.family].

Two citation grammars run side by side and never mix within a sentence - a numbered reference ('Looking at Figure 3', 'as follows in Table 1') for the four numbered figures and the tables, and pure deixis ('We see in the figure below', 'The lower curve above', 'This graph shows') for the five unnumbered charts [mention.lead_pattern].
Two of the nine figures are never cited at all - Figure 4 and the scenario-1 population curve on p20 - and both are the second member of a pair whose first member is discussed [mention.first_page].

One citation is mis-numbered: the p18 sentence that summarizes the gender/age weights reads 'summarized in Table 4' while Table 3 is the grid printed directly beneath it, so Table 3 is the only table no sentence names and Table 4 is announced twice, on p18 and again on p19 [mention.style].

Tables are announced one page before they print (p17 for p18, p18 for p19) while figures print on or after their lead page, so the table numbering and the figure numbering run on different displacements [mention.lead_pages].

Captions are longer than this lane's average - 11 to 14 words for the four figures, 5 to 13 for the four tables - and none states a unit, a condition or a conclusion, so length is spent on naming the experiment, not on interpreting it [caption.words].

Legends appear on four of the nine figures and only ever one way: a boxed inside legend at upper right on the two p6 screenshots, and an outside-right legend on the dissimilarity pair whose ten italic entries are wider than the plot they belong to [geometry.legend].

Nothing in the paper is three-dimensional, nothing carries a colourbar, and the only colour encoding is series hue - there is no sequential scale anywhere in nine figures and four tables [geometry.colorbar].

Two chart engines have two dialects: the MATLAB screenshots carry in-plot titles and 'Number of Citizens' / 'Elapsed Time in Years'-style axis titles with plain integer ticks, while the vector charts carry no plot title, paste the axis title at the end of the axis, and print space-separated thousands (20 000, 36 000) [geometry.printed_numbers].

The same experiment reported twice is not reported the same way: Figure 4 drops the in-plot title Figure 3 prints and shortens 'Dissimilarity Rating' to 'Dissimilarity' and 'Years' to 'Elapsed Time in Years', so the pair a reader will compare shares no axis word on either side [geometry.shared_axes].

Charts that need a key mostly do not get one: the p10 GDP scatter prints two fitted curves, linear and quadratic, with no legend to tell which is which, and the Lorenz curve prints two unlabelled curves side by side, leaving the prose to say 'the lower curve above' [geometry.legend].

All four grids are one style - a full outer box, a rule under the single header row and a rule between every body row - so the paper has no booktabs, no vertical-rules-only grid and no rule-less grid [table.rule_style].

No grid is shaded, none merges a cell, none has a two-tier header, none carries a diagonal split, and none prints a unit in the header - the tables are as uniform as the figures are not [table.merged_cells].
Not one table has a note line under its grid and not one continues onto a second page, so the four grids sit entirely inside the page their caption opens [table.continued].
Table width is the only table variable: 60 per cent of the text width for the two-column Likert scale against full width for the two five-metric grids, with no change of type size [table.width].
Only Table 4 has a decimal that wanders - its five-decimal 0.78709 sits right of the six-decimal cells around it - because no grid aligns on the decimal point at all [table.decimal_aligned].

Exhibit size is set by tool, not by importance: the four raster screenshots run 0.11 to 0.12 of a page, the five vector charts 0.05 to 0.09, and the smallest thing in the paper is Table 1's four-row Likert scale at 0.04 [place.area_frac].

Placement follows displacement: the two p6 figures sit at the top of the page because their lead sentence is on p5, and every chart whose lead is on the same page sits in the middle or foot of it - the only other top-of-page exhibit is the uncited Figure 4 [place.page_zone].

The summary sheet is a control page, not an exhibit: p1's whole-page block is the MCM summary form and is the paper's only excluded region, so 13 of the 14 measured regions are content [place.doc_order].
